newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's index of five top shares launched by IFC.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's index of five top shares launched by IFC.

text.p: The International Finance Corporation (IFC) has included Morocco in a stand alone index prior to its introduction in the Emerging Markets Investable Indexes, Upline Securities said on Tuesday.
The Washington-based IFC, which is the World Bank's financial arm, tracks 44 emerging markets and has two indices, the Global Index series and Investable Index series.

"After the inclusion of Morocco in the IFC Global Index last January, the corporation intends to introduce the kingdom in Investable Index through a stand alone index," Mohamed Mekouar, analyst at the Casablanca-based Upline told Reuters.

The stand alone index, which was introduced for Morocco on February 4, comprises five blue-chip stocks, including the largest conglomerates, ONA Group, Societe Nationale d'Investissement and leading Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur.
The two other stocks are Wafabank and Samir oil refinery, Mekouar said.
"To be included in the IFC stand alone index, the stocks have to respond to basic requirments of a market capitalisation of at least $50 million and $100 million annual turnover," Mekouar added.
"The decision to include the Moroccan market in the Investable Index series demonstrates the progress made in the expansion and major development of its bourse."

The impact of these indices will be particulary significant because IFC investable indexes are typically used by the fund managers to evaluate portfolio performances that will lead to the attraction of new portfolio investment flows to Morocco, Upline Securities said.
After a gloomy environment in 1995 due to negative effects of severe drought, the Casablanca stock exchange registered an excellent performance of 30.6 percent in 1996, a broker said.
The all-share index rose to 447.13 points in 1996 from 342.29 points in the previous year.
The market capitalisation also jumped 50 percent to 76.2 billion dirhams ($8.3 billion) in 1996, up from 50.8 billion dirhams in 1995.
"The bourse gained both in liquidity and volume due mainly to mutual funds, which collected more than 2.7 billion dirhams in 1996 against 1.0 billion dirhams in 1995," a market analyst said.
Total volume was 20.2 billion dirhams in 1996 against 23.2 billion dirhams in 1995, a bourse official said.
Established in 1929, the Casablanca bourse has 47 listed stocks, and 22 mutual funds.
